יש לכוין בעניית הקדיש: הגה ולא יפסיק בין יהא שמיה רבא למברך [הגהות אשר"י בשם א"ז כתב דלפי' ראשון לא יפסיק בין שמיה לרבא ולפירוש ר"י אין להפסיק בין רבא למברך] ולענות אותו בקול רם ולהשתדל לרוץ כדי לשמוע קדיש: הגה ויש לעמוד כשעונין קדיש וכל דבר שבקדושה ומי שבא לב"ה ושומע הקהל עונין קדיש עונ' עמהם אע"פ שלא שמע ש"צ שאמר יתגדל וכו' [הגהות חדשים במרדכי דברכות] וגם הש"צ צריך לומר יהא שמיה רבא וכשמתחיל יתגדל י"ל ועתה יגדל נא כח וגו' זכור רחמיך וגו':
mechaber.en: Laws of the Congregation's responding to the Kaddish (5 sections): One should have concentration when answering the Kaddish. and one should answer loudly and strive to run to hear Kaddish. {Rama: Rem"a: And one does not interrupt between "Y'hei Sh'meih Rabbah" ("May the Great Name") and "M'varakh" ("be blessed") [Hagahot Asheri in the name of Or Zarua wrote regarding the first explanation: "One should not interrupt between "Sh'meih" and "Rabbah" and according to the explanation of the Ri: one should not interrupt between "Rabbah" and "M'varakh"]. Rem"a: And one should stand when answering Kaddish and any davar she-bikdushah ("matter in which there is holiness" - a recitation which requires a minyan). And one who comes to synagogue and hears the congregation answering Kaddish answers along with them even though he did not hear the prayer-leader saying "Yitgadal etc." [Hagahot Chadashim on the Mordechai on Brakhot]. And the prayer-leader also needs to say "Y'hei Sh'meih Rabbah...". And when he begins "Yitgadal...", one should say "And now, let power [of YHVH] be magnified..." (Numbers 14:17) and "Remember Your mercy..." (Psalms 25:6).}

קדיש. איש"ר עדיף טפי מקדושה ומודים ע"כ אם שמע קדיש וקדושה או מודים וא"א לו לענות שניהם יענה איש"ר. באר שבע וכ"כ בתשובת שי למורא סימן ט' וכתב המ"א נ"ל דאם יש שתי בתי כנסיות לפניו בעיר באחד מגיעים לקדושה ובאחד לקדיש שאחר י"ח ילף ויענה קדושה כי שם ישמע גם כן קדיש אתר התפלה עיין סי' ק"ט. ואם התחיל לענות קדושה לא יפסיק בו לענות איש"ר. פרי חדש סי' קכ"ח:

baer_heitev.en:
The Kaddish. Sefer Chasidim wrote of an incident with one pious man who saw another pious man after his death, and his face was green. He said to him: why is your face green? He said to him: because I would speak while the shaliach tzibbur said Vayechulu, the blessing Magen Avot, and Yitgadal. In Mateh Moshe siman 411 he brought in the name of a Midrash that one sage appeared to his student in a dream, and the student saw that he had a mark on his forehead. He said to him: why did this happen to you? He said to him: because I was not careful not to speak when the chazzan said Kaddish.
To the blessed One. Mevarakh has a kamatz under the bet and a patach under the resh. Le'alam has a kamatz under the ayin. Shelah. Regarding ule'almei with a vav, see Beit Yosef. The Ba'er Heitev before me wrote le'almei without a vav in the name of the intentions of the Ari z"l, but this is not so; see there. Yitbarakh is without a vav. Di vera are two words. Min kol birkhata: see the writings on kavvanot and Yad Aharon.
Kaddish. Amen yehei shemei rabba is preferable to Kedushah and Modim. Therefore, if one hears Kaddish and Kedushah or Modim and cannot answer both, he should answer Amen yehei shemei rabba. Be'er Sheva; so too responsa Shay LaMora siman 9. Magen Avraham wrote: it appears to me that if there are two synagogues before him in the city, in one they are reaching Kedushah and in the other Kaddish after the Amidah, he should go and answer Kedushah, for there he will also hear Kaddish after the prayer; see siman 109. If he began answering Kedushah, he should not interrupt it to answer Amen yehei shemei rabba. Pri Chadash siman 128.
Kaddish. In Darkei Moshe he wrote that Maharil would not stand for Kaddish, but any Kaddish that caught him standing, he would remain standing until after Amen yehei shemei rabba. So wrote Shiyarei Knesset HaGedolah: I too practice like Maharil; see siman 58. So too in the book of the Ari's kavvanot it is written there: what appears from the Yerushalmi, that one must rise when answering Amen yehei shemei rabba, is a mistake, for it is not actually from the Yerushalmi, but one sage made it. See what Magen Avraham wrote. In the kavvanot there is a gloss as follows: the practice of my master z"l was that in all the Kaddishes after the Amidah of Shacharit, Minchah, and Ma'ariv he would remain standing. For Titkabel and for returning the Sefer Torah, he would answer and afterward sit; see there. See the book Nagid UMitzvah. Mahari Sarug z"l wrote that for the Kaddish of Shabbat evening one should stand.
Strength. The Ari z"l did not want to say it, and he almost mumbled, saying that it is not from the Tikkunim. Magen Avraham wrote: therefore one should not say it between Yishtabach and Yotzer, or between redemption and prayer, or in any place where it is forbidden to interrupt. Shelah and Bach. The chazzan returns and says Amen yehei shemei rabba even though he already said "and say Amen"; responsa Darkei Noam, Orach Chayim part 1 siman 18. See responsa Ne'eman Shmuel siman 1. But in Shiyurei Knesset HaGedolah he wrote that this is not proper; rather, the shaliach tzibbur returns to answer yehei shemei rabba, but not Amen yehei shemei rabba, for that is like answering Amen twice. See siman 61 seif 12 in the gloss and what is written there. See Halachot Ketanot part 1 siman 16.

chokhmat_shlomo.en: Seif 1: One should have kavanah when answering Kaddish, etc. NB: see in Taz note 1 what he wrote in the name of the Tur—that therefore Kaddish was instituted in the vernacular so the ministering angels would not be jealous of us, etc. And behold this appears alluded to in scripture, as the poet said: "He redeems my soul in peace from battles against me, for many were with me" (Psalms 55:19)—for there is a matter done above in a way of peace, and there is a matter that is not a way of peace. Regarding a matter in which there is no prosecution from the ministering angels, it is a way of peace; but what the ministering angels prosecute—since in any case their words are not heard—it is not done in peace but in dispute. Therefore prayer that comes in the holy tongue—if the prayer is accepted, nevertheless it is not a way of peace but in dispute; but prayer that comes in the vernacular, which the ministering angels do not understand and there is no prosecution from them—this comes in a way of peace. But behold, in other languages it helps only in public and not for an individual, as written below siman 101. Therefore prayer of an individual cannot be both together—a way of peace and that the prayer be accepted; necessarily, if he prays in the holy tongue there is prosecution from the ministering angels and it is not in peace; and if he prays in the vernacular the prayer is not heard at all. But in public you find both—that it will be in peace and the prayer will avail, such as praying in the vernacular. And this is what he said: "He redeems my soul in peace"—without prosecution from the ministering angels at all—and that is by virtue of "for many were with me": I stood and prayed in the vernacular and there was no prosecution and my prayer was accepted in peace—and it fits well; understand. May it be His will that it be so in the exile, and may their prayer of all the house of Israel be accepted, Amen.

kaf_hachayim.en: (1) [Se'if 1] One should have concentration when answering Kaddish, etc., and answer it in a loud voice, etc. For it is stated in tractate Shabbat, chapter Kol Kitvei, 119b: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said — whoever answers "amen, y'hei sh'meih rabbah m'varakh" with all his strength — they tear up his decree, etc. Rabbenu Yonah wrote in the chapter Mi sheMeto: meaning with all the power of his intention; and because there are people whose intention is not aroused except through force, it says "with all his strength" — but one need not raise a very loud voice so people mock him, until here. So too Rashi explained there, in Kol Kitvei: "with all his strength" — with all his intention. Tosafot wrote there, in Ri's name: it is stated in Pesikta in the story of Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha, who said there: when Israel enter synagogues and say "y'hei sh'meih rabbah m'varakh" in a loud voice, harsh decrees are annulled, until here. So too in Zohar, parashat Terumah 129b: "and to answer with strong might 'amen, y'hei sh'meih rabbah m'varakh,'" etc. — all this Rabbeinu Bechayei brought and wrote it appears one must answer in a loud voice. Thus the Zohar there: this holiness is not like other holinesses that we triple; but this holiness ascends on all sides above and below and on all sides of faith, and breaks iron locks and seals (meaning: stamps) and evil shells, to raise the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, over all; and we must say it in the language of the Other Side and answer with strong might "amen, y'hei sh'meih rabbah m'varakh," so the might of the Other Side is broken and the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, ascends over all. When it is broken in this holiness, the might of the Other Side — the Holy One, blessed be He, ascends in His glory and remembers His children and remembers His name. And because the Holy One, blessed be He, ascends in His glory in this holiness, it is only with ten; and in this language the Other Side is subdued against its will and its might is broken and the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, ascends, and iron locks and seals and strong chains and evil shells are broken, and the Holy One, blessed be He, remembers His name and His children. Fortunate are the holy people to whom the Holy One, blessed be He, gave the holy Torah to merit in the world to come, until here — Beit Yosef brought this. He wrote that from here one may reflect how much concentration is required in Kaddish and how much effort to answer it, until here. Therefore Maran ruled in Shulchan Aruch that one must do both — concentrate when answering Kaddish and also answer in a loud voice. Further in Zohar, parashat Bereishit 38b: thus — within this hall all those who sanctify with all the might of their Master's name stand and answer "amen, y'hei sh'meih rabbah m'varakh" with all might, and these stand within this hall; and that light comprising all colors shines for them; and from that light they exist and see other lights that unite and do not unite within them; and above them is Mashiach, who enters and stands over them and descends to them — he takes from this hall and enters, until here. Now you have been shown how great is the merit of answering Kaddish with intention and a loud voice; nevertheless one need not raise a very loud voice so people mock him, but raise his voice slightly with all his intention. See Ma'amar Mordechai letter gimel; Mishnah Berurah siman 2 letter lamed dalet; Siddur Beit Yosef on laws of answering Kaddish letter gimel; and below letter tet vav.

הקדיש עבה"ט. וכ' בבר"י בשם מהר"י מולכו בתשובות כת"י כשם שאסור לעבור נגד המתפלל כך אסור לעבור ננד האומר קדיש:
לברך. עבה"ט. ועיין ברכי יוסף דלפי מ"ש המג"א אין להפסיק לא בין שמיה לרבא ולא בין רבא למברך יש לגרוס ולא יפסיק בין שמיה רבא מברך וה"ג בל"ח. אך בד"מ לא הזכיר כ"א בין רבא למברך ע"ש ומ"ש הבה"ט מן כל ברכתא ובימים שכופלים בקדישים לעילא ולעילא א"ל מן רק מכל כדי שלא יהיה רק כ"ח תיבות ע"ש ולזה רמזו העונה אמן בכל כחו ומ"ש שאינו בכוונות לו' עלמיא בלא ו' המעיין שם ימצא שכן הוא וגם בש"ץ כ"כ לו' עלמיא בלא ו' ועיין בב"י שזה היה דעת מהר"י אבוהב:
קדיש עבה"ט. וכתב בר"י בשם מהר"י מולכו כשמתפללין בעזרת בה"כ בב' וג' מקומות ובעוד שזה אומר בחייכון זה אומר יתגדל וכיוצא וא"א לענות ב' וג' קדישים יענה על הראשון דוקא ע"ש. ויש למחות ביד הנוהגין לו' הקדיש עם הש"ץ בשעה שהוא מנגן וז"ל הרא"ש בתשובה כלל ד' סי' י"ט דבר פשוט הוא שא"ל קדיש עם החזן ע"ש והביאו בש"ץ:
עבה"ט ומ"ש דבקדיש ערבית של שבת יש לעמוד עיין בש"ץ שכתב שמהרח"ו בסידורו כתב דיש לקום בקדיש ברכו דערבית של שבת (ור"ל אותן הנוהגין לו' קדיש קודם ברכו של קבלת שבת) (ודלא כמשמעות הבה"ט דמשמע דעל הקדיש שאחר תפלת ערבית קאמר דז"א דזה דינו כשאר קדישים) ועיין בפע"ח בהגהות מהר"י צמח שלפי שהקדיש אחר קבלת שבת כשהוא עומד צריך להיות נשאר מעומד (ולפי מ"ש הש"ץ לאו מה"ט אתינן עלה) ששם קבלת הרוח ע"ש לכן בופרוס עלינו ששם קבלת הנשמה של שבת ע"ש ואפשר שר"ל שגם הקדיש של אחר ופרוס יהיה בעמידה משום זה:
כח. עבה"ט. ובבר"י כתב בשם מז"ה שכתב בשם צרור החיים שכתב יש בני אדם שאומרים ועתה יגדל כו' ושמעתי ממורי הרשב"א ששמע ממורינו הרמב"ן שלא אמר שום ענין אבל היה נוהג לו' זכור רחמיך ה' כו' לפי שאמרו בברכות בשעה שאומרים איש"ר כו' ע"ש ונראה דגם פסוק זה אין לו' כשעומד במקום שאין רשאי להפסיק:
shaarei_teshuvah.en:
Kaddish—Be'er Heitev. And so in Be'er Mayim Chayim in the name of Mahari Molcho in responsa manuscript: just as it is forbidden to pass before one praying, so it is forbidden to pass before one saying Kaddish.

M'varakh—Be'er Heitev. And see Birkei Yosef, for according to what Magen Avraham wrote one should not interrupt neither between sh'meih and rabbah nor between rabbah and m'varakh; the text should read "one should not interrupt between sh'meih rabbah m'varakh," and so in Lashon Chazal. But in Darkei Moshe he mentioned only between rabbah and m'varakh, as above. And what Be'er Heitev wrote "mikol birkhata," and on days when they double Kaddishes l'eila ul'eila, say only "mikol" so there not be only 28 words, as above; and therefore they hinted that one answering Amen with all one's might. And what he wrote that one not in kavanot say "almaya" without vav—the careful reader there will find it is so; and the shatz likewise says "almaya" without vav; and see Beit Yosef that this was Mahari Abuhav's view.

Kaddish—Be'er Heitev. And he wrote in Be'er Mayim Chayim in the name of Mahari Molcho: when praying in a large synagogue in two or three places, and while one says "bechayechon" another says Yitgadal and the like, one cannot answer two or three Kaddishes—one answers only on the first, as above. One should protest against those who say Kaddish with the shatz while he chants; and thus the Rosh in responsa klal 4 siman 19: it is a simple matter that one should not say Kaddish with the chazzan, as above; and they brought it in Shulchan Aruch.

Be'er Heitev—and what he wrote that for Shabbat Maariv Kaddish one should stand: see Shulchan Aruch, who wrote that Maharach wrote in his siddur one should stand for Kaddish Barchu of Shabbat Maariv (and he means those who say Kaddish before Barchu of kabbalat Shabbat) (and not as Be'er Heitev seems to imply, that he speaks of the Kaddish after Maariv tefillah—for that is like other Kaddishes). And see Pa'aneach Raza in Hagahot Mahari Tzemach, that since the Kaddish after kabbalat Shabbat, when standing, one must remain standing (and according to what Shulchan Aruch wrote we do not rely on Be'er Heitev for this), for there is kabbalat ruach, as above; therefore in Ufros Aleinu, for there is kabbalat neshamah of Shabbat, as above; and possibly he means that the Kaddish after Ufros should also be standing for this reason.

Koach—Be'er Heitev. And in Be'er Mayim Chayim he wrote in the name of Maharatz Chajes, who wrote in the name of Tzror HaChayim: some people say "ve'attah yigdal," etc.; and I heard from my teacher the Rashba, who heard from our teacher the Ramban, that he said no such thing, but would say "Zokhor rachamekha..." etc., because they said in Berakhot that when saying Amen yehei shmei rabbah, etc., as above; and it appears that this verse too one should not say when standing in a place where interruption is forbidden.
